storyboard.claim: Yalow's classmate scored 90s while she ground through late nights and still got 60s.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking over notes, the late-night grind shown by the library set.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the Yalow example from the previous chunk's setup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the effort gap the narrator describes, not just the grades.
storyboard.staging: Worried host with notes in a library: the grind, not the talent, is on screen.

storyboard.claim: Drive beat raw processing power.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target: drive aimed at a goal despite bad grades.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the Yalow story from the grades to her drive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the trait that won out over raw talent.
storyboard.staging: Host points at the target: her drive, not her raw power, is the point.

storyboard.claim: She kept working and eventually won the Nobel.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host raising a hand for the Nobel win.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the grades into the outcome.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the payoff of persistence explicit.
storyboard.staging: Celebrating host: the persistent path ends in the prize.

callout.text: Talent is just a sensory advantage

storyboard.claim: Talent is only a sensory advantage, not a full explanation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: None that reads literally; the callout carries the claim.
storyboard.onScreenText: Talent is just a sensory advantage
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from Yalow to what talent actually is.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the callout restates the narrator's definition of talent.
storyboard.staging: Host explaining; no icon, since a faster-clicking math idea has no clean literal picture.

storyboard.claim: Talent gets you a head start; drive gets you through the long process.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing at the starting line the narrator describes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the talent point to the starting line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Separates the head start from the long haul drive covers.
storyboard.staging: Host points forward: talent is the start, not the race.

storyboard.claim: Talent without drive gives up when the field rejects its first paper.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host slumped in defeat, the rejection outcome.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the failure case of talent alone.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the rejection moment as the point where talent quits.
storyboard.staging: Slumped host: talent alone gives up after the first rejection.

storyboard.claim: Talk is drifting toward the blank-slate view that grit alone wins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; no literal picture of a blank slate.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the objection to the drive argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the position the hosts are testing.
storyboard.staging: Host questioning: the objection is spoken, not pictured.

storyboard.claim: The claim that grit alone wins a Nobel is rejected.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking with the struck-through claim.
storyboard.onScreenText: Grit can win a Nobel (struck through)
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the blank-slate claim just raised.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejection visibly.
storyboard.staging: Host dismissing the claim: the strike shows it is false.

storyboard.claim: Talent sets real limits: no working memory, no ear for music.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking over the limits he lists.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concedes the blank slate is not blank.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the limits as the concession.
storyboard.staging: Thinking host conceding a limit.

storyboard.claim: Early prodigy talent is a terrible predictor of creative impact.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing at the predictor claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the limits into the key finding about prodigies.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the data finding in three words.
storyboard.staging: Host points at the claim: prodigy talent does not predict impact.

storyboard.claim: IQ is necessary up to about 120, enough to understand the domain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the number is carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the talent claim to IQ.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the threshold number.
storyboard.staging: Host explaining the threshold.

storyboard.claim: Beyond the threshold, more IQ does not mean more creativity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking with the struck-through equation.
storyboard.onScreenText: More IQ doesn't equal creativity (struck through)
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the threshold to the claim beyond it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the rejected equation.
storyboard.staging: Host rejecting the IQ equation.

storyboard.claim: The person must aggressively conquer the domain to reach the field.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor reaching toward the gatekeeper panel member.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the IQ point into the personality needed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the reach toward the gatekeeper.
storyboard.staging: Inventor reaching toward the gatekeeper: the field must be won over.

storyboard.claim: The personality needed to survive is not normal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; no literal picture of an abnormal personality.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Leads into the paradoxes that follow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the personality as unusual.
storyboard.staging: Host introducing the claim.

storyboard.claim: The paradox is complicated, and we like to put people in boxes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing as if at a list of categories.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the boxes the next beat names.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names our habit of categorizing.
storyboard.staging: Host pointing at the habit of boxing people.

storyboard.claim: People get sorted into neat boxes: introvert or extrovert, humble or arrogant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A four-bucket sorter of the labels the narration names.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Makes the boxes from the previous beat literal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the four pairs the narration lists.
storyboard.staging: Sorter diagram; host talking over the boxes.

storyboard.claim: Creative people do not live in the golden mean; they operate at extremes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking with the struck-through golden mean.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the middle the boxes suggested.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the mean as the creative home.
storyboard.staging: Host dismissing the middle ground.

storyboard.claim: Brenda Milner is an internationally renowned pioneer.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing to introduce Milner by name.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the example of the extremes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the case study the narration introduces.
storyboard.staging: Host introducing Milner with warmth for her legacy.

storyboard.claim: Milner is not celebrating; she is doing something else in her lab.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking with the struck-through champagne.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the expected celebration with what she is doing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the celebration reading.
storyboard.staging: Thinking host: the celebration is rejected, so no trophy is drawn.

storyboard.claim: She paces and tears her own recent work apart.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pacing, worried, as she tears work apart.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what she is doing instead of celebrating.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the self-destructive review through motion.
storyboard.staging: Worried pacing host: she is tearing her work apart.

storyboard.claim: Her internal monologue is a loop of anxiety and self-doubt.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking, worried, the anxiety loop.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the feeling behind the pacing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the monologue into two words.
storyboard.staging: Worried thinking host: the doubt is in the head.

storyboard.claim: Her doubt sits next to the fact she was in the room at all.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A door: the way into the room of the field.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From self-doubt to the access she still had.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door shows access to the field.
storyboard.staging: Thinking host beside the door: she got into the room.

storyboard.claim: Submitting the work took an almost staggering arrogance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing at the arrogance claim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the doubt into the arrogance it coexists with.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the opposite trait sharply.
storyboard.staging: Host points: arrogance and doubt live in the same person.

storyboard.claim: She believed she saw what the scientific world had missed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking in the office set of established experts.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the arrogance as seeing what others missed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the belief behind the audacity.
storyboard.staging: Host talking in the expert office: she challenged the established view.

storyboard.claim: Impostor feelings swing between thinking the work is brilliant and thinking it is trash.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance weighing brilliant against trash.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the arrogance and doubt into a swing.
storyboard.addedInformation: The balance shows the two sides being weighed.
storyboard.staging: Worried thinking host: the two verdicts are weighed.

storyboard.claim: The swing is not a flaw; it is the emotional engine of a creative personality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking with the struck-through flaw.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the flaw reading of the swing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the flaw framing.
storyboard.staging: Host dismissing the flaw reading.

storyboard.claim: Hans Bethe argued great physics takes long, painful thinking time.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing to introduce Bethe by name.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the next case with a named physicist.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the physicist the narration cites.
storyboard.staging: Host pointing to the named physicist.

storyboard.claim: Great problems can take years of deep thought, with no guarantee.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An hourglass: years passing on one problem.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bethe's point becomes the time it costs.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hourglass shows time passing.
storyboard.staging: Worried thinking host beside the hourglass.

storyboard.claim: You can come out of years of work with nothing: total failure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host slumped, sad, the failure outcome.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the risk the years of work carry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the outcome of failure plainly.
storyboard.staging: Sad slumped host: the failure is the cost.

storyboard.claim: Creators need the playful exploration of a child.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy scientist, playful at his bench.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the paradox: child play with endurance.
storyboard.addedInformation: The child embodies playful exploration.
storyboard.staging: Playful boy scientist: childlike exploration, the first half of the mix.

storyboard.claim: The work also needs the pain tolerance of an ultramarathon runner.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road: a long run of endurance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the endurance half of the mix.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road shows the long distance of the run.
storyboard.staging: Host walking the road: long endurance.

storyboard.claim: Living at those extremes sounds like a recipe for burnout.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host slumped, worried, the burnout risk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Raises the psychological risk of the extremes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the extremes as burnout risk.
storyboard.staging: Worried slumped host: the cost is burnout.

storyboard.claim: Creative people control the dial; it is not a mood disorder.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing with the struck-through mood disorder.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the disorder reading of the extremes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the disorder reading.
storyboard.staging: Host dismissing the disorder reading.

storyboard.claim: They shift between states based on what the system requires.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the callout names the adaptive shift.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the disorder reading with an adaptive one.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the mechanism of the shift.
storyboard.staging: Host explaining the adaptive shift.

storyboard.claim: In ideation they turn up playfulness and arrogance; no idea is too crazy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb: the spark of a new idea in brainstorming.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the phase-by-phase breakdown.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lightbulb marks the ideation spark.
storyboard.staging: Playful host celebrating a new idea.

storyboard.claim: When they must prove the idea, they flip the switch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the switch is named, not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from brainstorming to proof.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the switch between the two modes.
storyboard.staging: Host explaining the switch.

storyboard.claim: In editing and experiments they are ruthless and violently self-critical.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking, worried, the self-critical review.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The second mode after the switch.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the editing mode's tone.
storyboard.staging: Worried thinking host: the critical edit.

storyboard.claim: They adapt their personality to match the system's friction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the callout names the adaptation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the modes switch.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the friction as the cause.
storyboard.staging: Host explaining the adaptation.

storyboard.claim: The person bends between the domain's rules and the field's skeptical judgment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor pointing at the gatekeeper: rules versus judgment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the two forces of the friction.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the rules-judgment pair as two people.
storyboard.staging: Inventor pointing at the gatekeeper: the two forces meet.

storyboard.claim: The aha moment comes from bouncing between rules and gatekeepers, not from a solitary genius.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking with the struck-through solitary genius.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk by rejecting the lone-genius myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike rejects the myth the next chunk opens with.
storyboard.staging: Host dismissing the solitary genius; no lone figure drawn.
